planning_notes.title: Checkpoint x-axis: cumulative training action steps

Padding, action dimensions/tokens, and repeated diffusion or flow solver evaluations do not add action steps. planning_notes.title: Use the checkpoints that were saved

planning_notes.title: Loss curves and their interpretation

PSI and π0.5 can have different loss definitions and scales; show their native loss trajectories in separate panels rather than ranking models by raw loss magnitude. planning_notes.title: Simulator success across checkpoints
planning_notes.text: For each task and checkpoint, success rate is successful rollouts divided by total rollouts. Use the quantitative comparison’s simulator/assets, action timing, success criteria, and held-out reset distribution, with the same paired seeds and rollout budget across models and checkpoints. results.title: What the harder controls reveal
results.text: The original 50% test gave every tracker balanced accuracy 1.00. With arms moved to the successful-source pose, frozen-threshold balanced accuracy falls to 0.56 for DT and 0.50 for S3, DT+S3 and DINO. At 70% with common poses, S3 still ranks outcomes strongly (AUROC 0.972), compared with DT 0.611, DT+S3 0.889 and DINO 0.917, but all four frozen thresholds have balanced accuracy 0.50. All 90% branches succeed: each of those trackers recognizes only 4/12 with original arm poses, versus 12/12 after common-pose continuation. These controls expose threshold sensitivity and, for DT at 70%, degraded ranking.

results.title: Two independent difficulty factors
results.text: Branch at 50%, 70%, or 90% of recorded duration; compare the original endpoint with an additional 10 seconds of physical motion to the successful source arm pose. Six source scenes × three branch times × three action modes × two arm conditions = 108 paired observations. These are only six independent scenes, with two development and four test scenes.

results.title: Goal pairing and evaluation rules
results.text: All variants of a source share its initial scene and successful demonstration goal. Preserve original source splits, thresholds and DT+surprisal coefficients. No new calibration. Every saved-frame label was checked against ABC; arm-pose controls reach the common robot target. This reuses previously analyzed scenes, so it is a follow-up robustness diagnostic, not a fresh independent test set. The parked condition adds 10 seconds of physics; without an equal-duration no-motion control, differences cannot be attributed solely to arm alignment.

Simulator policy evaluation now uses PSI / Other Policy: either controller is sufficient, held fixed across PSI, real-world, and ABC physics environments. Both policy types are optional; other policy studies are unchanged.
Removed the familiar-scene reference-rollout task and requirement from the qualitative OOD evaluation.

Generalizability now shows LIBERO first with IND, 10-task OOD, and four-suite links (all /libero). All new qualitative and baseline comparison work is grouped under ABC. The existing LIBERO page supports all three completed evaluation entries.

Reorganized Generalizability into two evaluations: qualitative OOD/emergent policy results and comparison with baselines. Preserved baseline recipes and links; sample efficiency stays separate and steerability is unchanged. Baselines compare success on 4–5 fixed tasks; efficiency uses 1–2 of them.

Specified sample efficiency as success rate versus cumulative training action steps for PSI plus the policy-selected VLA and WAM on one or two ABC tasks. Added training/checkpoint/plot tasks; steerability remains unchanged for a later discussion.

Added a fourth policy goal: compare PSI with ACT, Diffusion Policy, Fast-WAM, and π0.5 or MolmoAct2 as alternative pretrained VLAs. Shared protocol and training plans are available; new training and evaluation remain incomplete.

Homepage now tracks the six experiments from the planning board with task-level statuses and direct results links. Existing LIBERO, ABC failure-identification, and public progress-tracking evaluations are linked as completed work; broader validation remains explicit.
Generalizability now contains LIBERO simulation evaluation and ABC. Existing LIBERO results remain available; ABC is a placeholder.
Research roadmap added from the planning board: six planned studies across policy, simulator, and progress. Existing LIBERO results linked under policy.
